experiment.title: SCE Experiment 3.5 - Detective Probe: Stolen Credential Attack-Chain Detection Validation
experiment.description: Validates that the detective controls for SCE node 3.5 fire correctly when attack nodes 1.2 (sts:AssumeRole on the EC2 instance-simulation role to obtain stolen instance-profile credentials, proxying the IMDS credential acquisition step of T1562.008 and T1552.005), 2.2 (sts:GetCallerIdentity with stolen credentials to verify credential validity and generate the identity-confirmation CloudTrail event of T1552.005), and 3.2 (iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies and s3:ListAllMyBuckets with stolen credentials to enumerate permissions and accessible resources, generating the lateral-movement reconnaissance CloudTrail events of T1078.004) are executed against IAM and S3 resources created in a clean AWS account. The experiment provisions a CloudTrail trail with CloudWatch Logs delivery enabled (providing a fast queryable signal), an S3 bucket for CloudTrail log storage with a service-principal bucket policy, a CloudWatch Log Group for the trail, a CloudTrail-to-CloudWatch Logs delivery IAM role, and an EC2 instance-simulation IAM role whose trust policy allows assumption from the same account to model stolen credential usage. All IAM resources are created directly via boto3 before CloudFormation is invoked. No Description field is passed to any IAM API call. GuardDuty is managed outside CloudFormation to tolerate pre-existing detectors. The detective probe confirms three independent signals within a 30-minute SLA: (A) GuardDuty raises a CredentialAccess:IAMUser/AnomalousBehavior, Recon:IAMUser/UserPermissions, or UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/InstanceCredentialExfiltration finding after the attack-chain API calls are made with the stolen credentials (ADT node 3.3), (B) the CloudTrail CW Logs delivery pipeline contains at least two of the four expected attack-chain event names (AssumeRole, GetCallerIdentity, ListAttachedRolePolicies, ListBuckets) confirming the SIEM correlation chain has the data to link Steps 1 through 3 (ADT node 3.3), and (C) the CloudTrail lookup_events API returns an AssumeRole event that references the instance-simulation role confirming the credential acquisition event is durably recorded as the audit-trail anchor for the full attack chain (ADT nodes 1.3 and 3.3). Rollback stops the CloudTrail trail, empties the S3 bucket, deletes the CloudFormation stack, deletes all boto3-created IAM roles, and deletes the GuardDuty detector only if this experiment created it.

steady-state-hypothesis.title: All three detective signals confirmed within 30-minute SLA: GuardDuty credential-access finding, CloudTrail attack-chain events in CW Logs, and CloudTrail AssumeRole event for instance role

probes.name: Verify GuardDuty CredentialAccess or Recon finding, at least two attack-chain event types in CloudTrail CW Logs delivery, and sts:AssumeRole event for instance role in CloudTrail lookup - all confirmed within 30-minute SLA after attack nodes 1.2, 2.2, and 3.2

method.name: Get-or-create GuardDuty detector; create CloudTrail CW delivery role and instance-simulation role via boto3 (no Description field); deploy CloudFormation stack with CloudTrail trail (CW Logs delivery enabled), S3 trail bucket, and CloudWatch Log Group; wait for trail IsLogging=True; assert detective baseline

Node 1.2: sts:AssumeRole on instance-simulation role to obtain stolen credentials (T1562.008 proxy); Node 2.2: sts:GetCallerIdentity with stolen credentials to verify identity (T1552.005); Node 3.2: iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies and s3:ListAllMyBuckets with stolen credentials for lateral movement enumeration (T1078.004)

rollbacks.name: Stop CloudTrail trail; empty S3 trail bucket; delete CloudFormation stack (trail, CW log group, S3 bucket); delete boto3-created IAM roles; delete GuardDuty detector only if created by this experiment; tolerant of missing resources
